name: Ahmet
presentingProblem: My girlfriend said she's going to leave me if I don't get help. I guess I'm too emotional. One minute I think she's the best thing that ever happened to me, the next I'm sure she's lying to me. I can't make it stop.
backstory: Ahmet is a 26-year-old graphic designer living in Istanbul. He grew up with a mother whose moods were unpredictable — warm and doting one day, cold and rejecting the next — and a father who worked long hours and stayed emotionally distant. As a Turkish man, Ahmet has internalized the stigma that 'real men don't fall apart,' which makes therapy itself feel shameful. He has had three serious relationships since age 18, each one following the same arc: intense connection, then accusations of betrayal, then explosive arguments, then desperate reconciliation. He has cut off long-term friendships abruptly when he felt slighted. He drinks more than he wants to and has driven recklessly after fights. He is intelligent and articulate when calm, but in session he is rarely calm for long.

coreBeliefs: I am defective in a way that cannot be fixed
intermediateBeliefs: If someone really sees me, they will leave
If I don't react strongly, no one will take my pain seriously
Closeness always ends in betrayal — so I have to test it before it tests me
automaticThoughts: She didn't text back — she's already done with me
He was nice to her at the café, he's probably attracted to her
You're judging me right now, I can see it on your face
Wait — you actually get it. You're the only one who gets it
I'm a disaster. Why would anyone stay?
triggers: Any perceived sign that the therapist is bored, judging, or distracted
Being asked to slow down or breathe (feels dismissive)
defenses: Splitting (sudden idealization of the therapist followed by devaluation)
Seeks reassurance intensely when feeling unsafe
Tests boundaries to see if the therapist will stay
Acts before thinking, then feels deep shame afterward
values: Creative expression through his design work
